audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Darius/Darius/Skill/Darius/Skill/Darius/Darius and hand Darius the three late stages outright. The content whys underneath say the opposite from Level 6 on ('By 6 his Sap Magic healing out-paces your Hemorrhage bleed', 'First-item tank stats let him heal through your AD trades', 'Two items in... Maokai unkillable for you'), and the packet levelChart is Darius x4 then Maokai x3.
audit.why: Nothing in Maokai's kit beats a Darius walk-up before 6 — Bramble Smash is 7s of knockback and slow, Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1. What flips it is sustain plus tank items, and that flip is permanent, which is why the lane sits at 49.4% over 1,330 games.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Darius through Levels 4-5, Maokai from Level 6 on, as one atomic group across both layers, with the Level 3, Level 6, First item and 2+ items whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase was generic Guillotine boilerplate carrying raw LaTeX ('R = d + a \times Stacks'), and the first-item phase was Stridebreaker boilerplate — neither says what actually changes at those two timings against Maokai.
audit.why: At 6 the thing that decides your ultimate is Twisted Advance, not the execute maths. At first item the thing that decides the lane is Sap Magic plus tank stats, not your Stridebreaker.
audit.corrected: Level 6 phase now covers the untargetable dash eating a Guillotine cast; First item phase now covers Sap Magic and anti-heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance is described throughout as just 'his lock-on root'. The page never states that Maokai is UNTARGETABLE during the dash.
audit.why: Riot: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target.' Noxian Guillotine is a targeted leap onto an enemy champion — so a Maokai who W's as you cast it takes the cast off you for nothing. That single fact changes when a Darius presses R in this matchup: on his landing, not on his takeoff.
audit.corrected: tldr, phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns and content spikes[1] now state the untargetable window and re-time the execute around it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells you to 'anti-heal his passive' but never says what actually drives Sap Magic — and content spikes[2] attributes the heal to the wrong ability entirely ('his W passive heal on ability hits').
audit.why: Riot: 'Each time Maokai casts a spell OR IS STRUCK BY AN ENEMY'S SPELL, this cooldown is reduced.' Your own Decimate and Apprehend hits accelerate the heal you are trying to out-race, so a long spell-heavy rotation is self-defeating without Grievous Wounds already applied. The heal is on Sap Magic (P); Twisted Advance (W) heals nothing.
audit.corrected: winCon, breakdown.early, phases[5].why, content mid and spikes[2] now state the spell-hit cooldown reduction and put Grievous Wounds before the chip, not after it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bramble Smash's knockback is mentioned once in the tldr and nowhere in the trading or cooldown advice, even though it is the shortest cooldown in the matchup.
audit.why: Bramble Smash 'knocks back nearby enemies... and slow[s] them' on 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s. Against Darius that is a repeatable tool for breaking a run-down and pushing you out of Decimate's blade range — it comes back roughly four times per Apprehend.
audit.corrected: phases[2].why now frames Level 3 as a displacement race (his knockback vs your pull) and breakdown.cooldowns carries the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave has swallowed two other sections — 'Key Mechanical Cooldowns' and 'How Darius Wins Trades' are pasted inside it, between 'Best wave' and 'Worst wave'.
audit.why: MatchupCoach.dc.html builds the wave boxes by slicing breakdown.wave between the literal markers 'Best wave', 'Worst wave' and 'Crash timing'. The interleaved text lands inside the 'Best wave' box, so the reader gets a paragraph of cooldown and trading advice under a wave-management heading.
audit.corrected: Not edited — repairing it means deleting roughly 700 characters, which no ±10% edit can express. Flagged for the user.

edits.before: Maokai roots you with W and sustains with saplings + passive. Dodge the W, anti-heal, and stick him between his shields. Low 1v1 threat. Don't chase past the wave into Twisted Advance (Root).
edits.after: Maokai roots you with Twisted Advance and sustains off Sap Magic. Land Grievous Wounds before you chip, because every spell you hit him with shortens that heal's own cooldown. Low 1v1 threat early.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it. Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane.
edits.after: - Twisted Advance (W): 14s at rank 1, and he is untargetable for the whole dash — a Guillotine cast into it is wasted. - Bramble Smash (Q): 7s at rank 1 down to 5s at rank 5, and the knockback pushes you off your Decimate blade. - Sapling Toss (E): 18s at rank 1, 1100 range, stronger in brush. - Apprehend: 26s at rank 1 — never throw it predictably.

edits.after: With first-item tank stats (Sunfire/Bami plus Sap Magic, whose cooldown falls every time your spells strike him) Maokai out-sustains your Hemorrhage bleed — you chunk him, he heals it back off minions, and the trade nets his way.
